scope_entries.finding: Three ways to reach an external HTTP service exist: http.call on a service actor with params.http.allow (no new code, synchronous, 64 KiB body cap, untyped); an agent actor with bridge_url speaking the cultureagent bridge protocol (async, callback, no new code); or a new package under culture_rules/extensions/ with typed kinds, a port, an optional /hooks/ route and event types. APP_SURFACES is a hardcoded tuple of five. No plugin discovery exists: every extension is in builtin.py. There is no generic POST /events; events come in by webhook route or the MQTT bus.

scope_entries.surface: jira-devague repo and culture-rules docs/operations/jira-conversations.md, docs/deliveries/2026-11-13-jira-devague-spec.md
scope_entries.finding: jira-devague is a separate stdlib CLI repo, installed as a uv tool on core, reached through runner commands and a Claude bridge operate agent. Actors, the bridge unit, grants, rules and workflows are live-only. Its safety rests on an operator-held command-prefix allowlist and env vars. 'bridge' in culture-rules today means the cultureagent agent-session bridge, not an app.

scope_entries.surface: PR fixer records (docs/specs/2026-11-06-no-flow-specific-code.md, docs/deliveries/2026-10-06-pr-fixer-rule.md, CHANGELOG.md:131)
scope_entries.finding: The PR fixer was a PR-driven agent flow coded into the engine, switched off live on 2026-10-19 and removed in 0.43.0. Its lessons on bot noise, self-authored comments, attempt caps and same-repo PRs apply to any new PR-driven flow.

scope_entries.surface: qodo-cli docs/qodo-skills-sources.md and docs/specs/2026-06-16-*.md
scope_entries.finding: The first spec's non-goals exclude reimplementing Qodo's server-side analysis and an interactive login.

scope_entries.surface: culture-rules app framework (culture_rules/server, auth, mcp, client, hatch_build.py, web/) and agentfront, culture-agent-template, citation-cli, guildmaster
scope_entries.finding: The citable parts are static.py (104 lines), auth (about 1,050 lines), mcp (about 190 lines), the verb registry with its parity test, hatch_build.py and the culture-design tokens. server/app.py and service.py are rules-specific. xteink already cites auth/access.py with recorded provenance and has the API, MCP and web triple; culture-library and pocketsync are smaller precedents. Only a python-cli reference exists in .teken/reference.

scope_entries.surface: culture_rules/actors/agent.py, extensions/llm, docs/actors/llm.md, lobes-cli README
scope_entries.finding: cortex is a lobes model lane (27B Qwen), addressed as a model through the lobes gateway. llm.complete gives text only. A bridge agent step gets a checkout from repo, head_branch and head_sha, can commit, and reports commits and changed files; the operate sandbox is actor-pinned and shipped only in the Claude bridge (cultureagent 0.17.0). No committed bundle holds a bridge agent actor.

scope_entries.surface: embedding precedents (culture_rules/, web/src, culture-library routes_web.py:37, pocketsync web/server.py:72, irc-lens web/app.py:60)
scope_entries.finding: No iframe, postMessage, shared shell or embedding design doc exists in culture-rules or its siblings. Each app has its own hostname behind Cloudflare Access, and three siblings forbid framing with frame-ancestors 'none'. Embedding is new work, and its meaning is undecided.

scope_entries.surface: cultureagent README.md:36-43 (agent bridges)
scope_entries.finding: Three stdlib HTTP bridges ship: qwen (Qwen Code over ACP), codex and claude. They never push. No Pi bridge exists in this checkout (git log head e7f7028/0.15.1, which may be behind the 0.17.0 the Jira records cite).

scope_entries.surface: http.call as the only link (culture_rules/extensions/http/port.py)
scope_entries.finding: Configuration-only access to the bridge goes through http.call on an actor with params.http.allow: synchronous, one request per step, response body capped at 64 KiB, loopback reachable only when that exact IP is allowlisted, auth by a grant-resolved header. There is no generic POST /events, so the bridge cannot push an event in without the MQTT bus; the Qodo-review-landed trigger is the existing GitHub review and comment events filtered by author in a rule condition.

scope_entries.surface: qodo-cli open issues 18 and 22
scope_entries.finding: Issue 18 (from devex-cli) asks for a public Python API, qodo.api, because the useful logic sits in private modules qodo.cli._providers and qodo.cli._qodo_api and devex drives main() and re-parses stdout. Issue 22 is titled 'mass-update: deterministic update'; its body was not read.

scope_entries.surface: Qodo public docs (docs.qodo.ai: agentic-toolbox/mcp, qodo-tools-reference, code-review/use-qodo-in-prs, configuration/configuration-file, governance/rule-enforcement, account-management/manage-api-keys, pricing-and-usage)
scope_entries.finding: Read through web fetch summaries, so wording is paraphrase. Documented: a remote MCP server with PR findings, mark-implemented, dismiss, rules search/list/get, merged-PR review history and codebase tools; /agentic_review as the trigger comment; ignore_bot_pr default true; .pr_agent.toml on the default branch, a wiki page, a pr-agent-settings repo and the portal as configuration sources; rules created in the portal, imported from AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, or mined from PR history; analytics as dashboard and CSV only. Not documented: webhooks, a REST reference, rules write over HTTP, check runs for a finished review, bot-posted commands. Personal API keys expire after at most 365 days; trial workspaces get 100 reviews a day.

scope_entries.surface: cultureagent origin/main (0.17.0, cultureagent/bridges/) and pi 1.5.2 on this machine
scope_entries.finding: Upstream has bridges claude, codex and qwen over one shared core (cultureagent/bridges/core) and no Pi bridge. pi 1.5.2 offers --print for a non-interactive run, --mode json or rpc, and 'pi mcp' to manage MCP servers.

scope_entries.surface: associate (installed 0.9.0, /home/ori/git/associate README.md, 'associate run --help')
scope_entries.finding: associate is a multi-model harness on Pi. 'associate run [prompt] --checkout DIR --timeout S --json' runs one task headless (default timeout 900 s); its cortex model may change the checkout behind a decider safety gate, and nothing is ever pushed. The repo README also lists --model and --test-command, which the installed 0.9.0 help does not show. culture-rules has a one-shot adapter for 'colleague work' (culture_rules/actors/agent.py:167) and none for associate; a registered runner command could run it with no code change.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: associate README (safety gate, never pushes) and the improvement flow in the spec
scope_entries.finding: An agent with write access to a checkout reads text written by PR authors and by a third-party bot, and its output becomes a PR that changes how the reviewer behaves. The spec had no human gate, repo allowlist or path limit on that output.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / unstated-assumptions lens: c24 against qodo/cli/_providers.py (gh) and parked v1
scope_entries.finding: c24 assumed a bot-authored PR. qodo-cli has no token handling and relies on the caller's gh login, so the author would be a person and ignore_bot_pr would not apply. The GitHub identity is undecided and now blocks.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / data-flow lens: culture_rules/extensions/github/hooks.py:84-96, 450-459
scope_entries.finding: The webhook receiver maps only created and submitted actions; an edited issue comment is answered 'ignored'. Qodo's docs say a push re-review updates the existing comment, so later reviews raise no event. One review also raises several events (comment, inline comments, review).

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / hidden-dependencies lens: http.call body cap (culture_rules/extensions/http/port.py, DEFAULT_MAX_BODY 64 KiB)
scope_entries.finding: A PR's full findings with agent prompts and suggestions can exceed 64 KiB, and http.call truncates silently into a 'truncated' flag.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency and operations lens: the merged-PR flow in the spec
scope_entries.finding: The spec's signal covers 1 merged PR. Nothing bounded the rate: every merge would start an agent run and could open another PR, and two runs could share a checkout.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: qodo-cli issue 18 (devex-cli integration)
scope_entries.finding: devex-cli calls qodo.cli.main with --json and parses stdout. Moving logic into qodo.api can break it if output shapes shift.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: qodo-cli pyproject.toml:22-23 and Qodo's CLI docs
scope_entries.finding: Both programs install a binary named qodo. 'which -a qodo' on this machine finds none installed, so the clash is not live here.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / observability and security lens: culture_rules/auth (two listeners, roles) and Qodo's key expiry (docs.qodo.ai manage-api-keys)
scope_entries.finding: The spec named the auth parts to cite but set no rule that routes need them, and nothing would show an expired personal key, which stops both flows silently.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / rollback and migration lens: docs/operations/rollout.md:20-24 (bundle shape, release.json)
scope_entries.finding: A bundle's optional release.json must name the culture-rules release, which would tie a bundle kept in qodo-cli to one culture-rules version; without it nothing states compatibility.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / unexamined surfaces
scope_entries.finding: Not examined: the associate repo beyond its README and run help (contract, gate, CLAUDE.md); Qodo's live MCP server (no call made); culture-rules http.call and rollout code (read by a survey agent, not re-read in this pass); the qodo-cli web UI and server, which do not exist yet; lobes gateway routing between core and spark.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / depth
scope_entries.finding: Rigorous, on the security-sensitive signal: a service holding a personal API key and GitHub credentials, and an agent with write access fed untrusted text. No data-loss, migration or hardware signal applies.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / reversibility lens: CHANGELOG.md:131 and culture_rules/extensions/github (client.py:340-368, port.py)
scope_entries.finding: The engine's GitHub client has get_pull, merge_pull, delete_ref and branch_tip only; a push kind existed and was removed in 0.43.0. Opening a PR as the App is new client and port code inside the github extension, and it changes the pinned github-app actor when listed in params.actions.

lapses.what: The Qodo capabilities in c22, c23, c24 and c26 rest on fetched summaries of Qodo's docs, not on a call to Qodo's MCP server or a test PR, and they were confirmed as assumptions without a live check.
lapses.skipped_check: a live tools/list call and one test PR

lapses.what: c24 says a bridge-opened configuration PR is skipped by ignore_bot_pr without checking who authors the PR: qodo-cli acts through a person's gh login, so the PR would be a person's, not a bot's.
lapses.skipped_check: checking the PR author identity against the setting's meaning

lapses.what: t4's agent wrote its tests before the code but never ran them failing first; they were first run after the implementation existed (one then failed and was fixed)
lapses.skipped_check: run the new tests red before implementing

lapses.skipped_check: diff stdout and exit codes against the pre-change CLI

lapses.skipped_check: write the tests first and see every one fail

obligations.seam: the culture_rules/ source tree
obligations.behavior: It contains no occurrence of the word qodo, in any case, after the work.
obligations.source_text: culture-rules connects surfaces and can call APIs, and it does not know the word qodo: no Qodo extension package, no Qodo action kind, no Qodo event namespace and no Qodo literal in culture_rules/. The configuration (actors, rules, workflows) knows Qodo and defines how to work with it. Anything culture-rules lacks to call the bridge is added as a generic capability.

obligations.seam: qodo-cli installed with no extras
obligations.behavior: It installs zero third-party packages and every existing verb runs; importing qodo never imports the server, MCP or web parts.
obligations.source_text: qodo-cli's runtime dependencies stay empty (pyproject.toml dependencies = [], best_practices.md:11-14). The server, MCP and web parts sit behind optional extras and are imported lazily, as culture-rules does with its server and mcp extras.

obligations.seam: a merged PR that carries the bridge's mark, arriving at the improvement rule
obligations.behavior: It starts no improvement run.
obligations.source_text: The bridge marks every configuration PR it opens (a fixed branch prefix and a label), and the improvement rule's condition excludes PRs carrying that mark.

obligations.seam: the qodo bridge's calls to GitHub
obligations.behavior: It never merges and never pushes to a default branch; a repo outside its allowlist is refused before any GitHub request.
obligations.source_text: The bridges never merge and never push to a default branch. A configuration change reaches a repo only as a PR a person reviews and merges, and only on repos in an allowlist the bridge holds.

obligations.seam: the associate checkout handed to the qodo bridge's propose verb
obligations.behavior: A diff touching any path outside the Qodo configuration allowlist, or files that fail validation, yields a refusal and no PR.
obligations.source_text: Text from PRs, Qodo findings and review history is untrusted input to the improvement agent. Before opening a PR the qodo bridge checks that the change touches only an allowlist of Qodo configuration paths and that the files validate, and refuses otherwise.

obligations.seam: GitHub review and comment events arriving at the opened-PR flow
obligations.behavior: One Qodo review starts exactly 1 run per PR head commit; the App's own comments and other bots start none.
obligations.source_text: The opened-PR flow starts from created events only (github.review.submitted, github.comment.created or github.review_comment.created by Qodo's login) and runs once per PR head commit, however many events one review produces. Re-reviews that edit an existing comment are out of the first version.

obligations.seam: a bridge API response read by an http.call step
obligations.behavior: It is under 64 KiB and carries counts, ids, statuses and URLs, not full finding text.
obligations.source_text: Bridge API responses meant for workflow steps are small: counts, ids, statuses and URLs, under the 64 KiB http.call body cap. Full findings stay in the bridge and its UI.

obligations.seam: the improvement flow acting on one repo
obligations.behavior: At most 1 configuration PR is open per repo, runs for one repo do not overlap, and each run has its own checkout.
obligations.source_text: At most 1 open configuration PR per repo: while one is open, a new improvement run for that repo ends without opening another. Improvement runs for one repo are serialized, and each run works in its own fresh checkout.

obligations.seam: qodo-cli --json stdout read by devex-cli
obligations.behavior: The output shape of rules, review, config and doctor is unchanged.
obligations.source_text: The --json output of qodo-cli's existing verbs (rules, review, config, doctor) does not change shape; devex-cli binds to it in-process (qodo-cli issue 18).

obligations.seam: the CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces of a bridge
obligations.behavior: Every verb exists on all three, and a parity test fails when one is missing.
obligations.source_text: Every bridge verb is reachable 3 ways (CLI, MCP tool, HTTP operation) and a parity test fails when 1 of the 3 is missing.

obligations.seam: a caller without a token at any bridge route that reads findings, changes a finding or opens a PR
obligations.behavior: It gets 401 and no data.
obligations.source_text: Both flows can be stopped in one step and leave nothing behind: disabling the bundle's rules stops new runs, the bridges hold no state culture-rules depends on, and the bundle states the lowest culture-rules version it needs.

obligations.seam: the surfaces' use of qodo-cli internals
obligations.behavior: CLI handlers, MCP tools and HTTP routes call qodo.api and import no private qodo.cli._ module.
obligations.source_text: The bridge's API, MCP tools and CLI verbs are thin layers over one public Python API in qodo-cli, the qodo.api module that qodo-cli issue 18 asks for, so the three surfaces cannot drift.

obligations.seam: associate and the git remote
obligations.behavior: associate changes files in its checkout only and never pushes or opens a PR.
obligations.source_text: associate is approved as the improvement agent, and it gets a bridge like qodo-cli does: the full set of surfaces, CLI, MCP server, HTTP API and web UI, built on the same bridge framework, which a culture-rules workflow reaches through configuration.

obligations.seam: source files in qodo-cli, associate and culture-rules
obligations.behavior: None holds the improvement agent's instruction text; it is read from configuration at run time.
obligations.source_text: No prompt lives in code. Instructions for the agent that improves the Qodo configuration are an actor brief (llm.complete) or step configuration (a bridge agent step's instruction), per CLAUDE.md 'No prompts in code' and docs/actors/llm.md:172-191.

obligations.seam: a workflow acting on an opened PR
obligations.behavior: It posts no /agentic_review or other Qodo command in the first version.
obligations.source_text: The first version does not trigger Qodo reviews; it relies on Qodo's automatic review on PR open.

obligations.seam: the bridge framework files cited into qodo-cli and associate
obligations.behavior: Each carries a header with its culture-rules source path and commit, and none contains app-specific code.
obligations.source_text: The bridge framework is assembled by citing culture-rules' generic parts into qodo-cli, since no shared reference for a server, an MCP server or a web shell exists: server/static.py (SPA serving), auth/access.py, resolve.py, tokens.py and principal.py (Cloudflare Access on loopback, service tokens on LAN, roles), mcp/server.py and tools.py with the verb registry and tests/test_surface_parity.py, the OpenAPI pin, hatch_build.py and web/src/culture-design. agentfront (formerly teken) derives only a CLI, a one-tool MCP and markdown pages, with no auth and no web app.

obligations.seam: a merged PR carrying the configuration mark (branch prefix and label), arriving at the improvement rule
obligations.behavior: It starts no improvement run.
obligations.source_text: Every configuration PR is opened with a fixed branch prefix and a label, set in the workflow's step configuration and not by the agent, and the improvement rule's condition excludes PRs carrying that mark.

obligations.seam: the bridges and GitHub repositories
obligations.behavior: No bridge pushes, merges or opens a PR; the only writer is culture-rules' App through the open-PR action, on repos in the App actor's allowlist.
obligations.source_text: The bridges never write to GitHub repositories: no push, no merge, no PR. A configuration change reaches a repo only as a PR that culture-rules' App opens on a repo in the App actor's allowlist, and that a person reviews and merges.

obligations.seam: a caller without a token at any bridge route that reads findings, changes a finding or proposes a configuration change
obligations.behavior: It gets 401 and no data.
obligations.source_text: No bridge route that reads findings, changes a finding or proposes a configuration change answers without authentication. culture-rules reaches the bridge with a service token held as a grant.

obligations.seam: the generic open-PR action and a repository
obligations.behavior: It commits only the given files to a new branch, never to the default branch, refuses a repo outside the allowlist, and a retried step opens no second PR.
obligations.source_text: culture-rules gains one generic GitHub action that opens a PR as the App: given a repo in the actor's allowlist, a new branch name, file paths with contents, a title, a body and labels, it commits the files to the new branch (never the default branch) and opens the PR. Its name, params and docs do not mention Qodo, and it follows the all-surfaces rules for a new action kind (catalogue fixture, docs/actors/github.md, tests).

obligations.behavior: They contain no occurrence of the word qodo and the action is usable for any repo file.
obligations.source_text: culture-rules gains one generic GitHub action that opens a PR as the App: given a repo in the actor's allowlist, a new branch name, file paths with contents, a title, a body and labels, it commits the files to the new branch (never the default branch) and opens the PR. Its name, params and docs do not mention Qodo, and it follows the all-surfaces rules for a new action kind (catalogue fixture, docs/actors/github.md, tests).

obligations.behavior: The package installs qodo-cli and no command named qodo; importing the Python package qodo still works.

obligations.seam: a caller without a token at any bridge route that reads findings, changes a finding or proposes a configuration change
obligations.behavior: It gets 401 and no data.
obligations.source_text: No bridge route that reads findings, changes a finding or proposes a configuration change answers without authentication. culture-rules reaches the bridge with a service token held as a grant.

obligations.behavior: A PR open and a PR merge start 0 runs, and no bridge state has to be cleaned up.
